# `attr structured` for [core](/commands/categories/core.md)

<div class='command-title'>Attribute for getting structured output from an external command.</div>

## Command Type

`built-in`

## Signature

```> attr structured {flags} (args) (decode)```

## Parameters

 -  `args`: Arguments that make the external command print structured output.
 -  `decode`: Turns that output, given as `$in`, into data.


## Input/output types:

| input   | output                                      |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| nothing | record&lt;args: list&lt;string&gt;, decode: closure&gt; |
## Examples

Get the changed files from `git status --porcelain` as a table.
```nu
> @structured [--porcelain] { lines | parse --regex '^(?<status>..) (?<file>.+)$' }
    extern "git status" []
    git status | where status =~ M | get file

```

Get the installed Python packages from `pip list --format=json` as a table.
```nu
> @structured [--format=json] { from json }
    extern "pip list" []
    pip list | where name starts-with num

```

Get the outdated Homebrew formulae from `brew outdated --json=v2` as a table.
```nu
> @structured [--json=v2] { from json | get formulae }
    extern "brew outdated" []
    brew outdated | where pinned == false | get name

```

Get pods from kubectl as a table when the output is piped into `where`.
```nu
> @structured [-o json] { from json | get items }
    extern "kubectl get" [resource: string, --namespace(-n): string]: nothing -> table
    kubectl get pods | where status.phase != Running

```

## Notes
When the output of the extern is used by nushell (piped into an internal command or collected into a variable), the arguments are added right after the command's name and the output is decoded with the block. When the output goes to the terminal, `print`, a file, `ignore`, `save`, `tee`, `complete` or another external command (`run-external` included), the command runs as written. The same holds when the extern is the last command of a `do` block or a custom command. Calling the command with a caret, like `^git status`, always runs it as written.

The arguments come before the user's own, so a format flag the user passes can override them and break the decode, as in `kubectl get pods -o wide`. Use a caret call for that. `tee` passes the command's own output on to the commands after it. When an extern has more than one `@structured`, the last one is used.

Like a `def` body, the block can read `$in`, `$env`, constants and the `let` variables declared before the extern, but not `mut` variables.
